3.0.s.en: 1. The descendants of David in Hebron

3.0.0.en: 1 Now these were the sons of David, which were born unto him in Hebron; the firstborn Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; the second Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess: 2 The third, Absalom the son of Maachah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur: the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith: 3 The fifth, Shephatiah of Abital: the sixth, Ithream by Eglah his wife. 4 These six were born unto him in Hebron; and there he reigned seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years.

3.0.1.en: Now these were the sons of David, which were born unto him in Hebron;

3.0.2.en: the firstborn Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;

3.0.3.en: the second Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess: [1]

3.0.4.en: In speaking of the descendants of David, he began with the firstborn Amnon [1] and ended with Tamar [9]. Amnon was the firstborn according to the flesh, and he was the shame of his father's house, so it was necessary to set him aside.

3.0.5.en: All the sons of David who were born before the full establishment of the monarchy are under a general judgment, such as Amnon and Absalom, because of corruption, rebellion and pride. These fell under judgment. The monarchy had to reach Jerusalem specifically, and the choice was according to grace (Ps 132:13).

3.1.0.en: Shimea, Shobab and Nathan are mentioned as the sons of Bathsheba, but they disappear so that Solomon, the youngest son, may come. Moreover, all the other sons who came after him had no right to the kingship[2].

3.1.1.en: In the Septuagint the list of the royal tribe was extended to about the year 250 B.C., which is the time of the translation itself.

3.1.2.en: The text points to the names of the mothers of six sons of David, who were born in Hebron before the transfer of his capital to Jerusalem (993 B.C.). Here the descendants of David begin with his sons in Hebron.

3.1.3.en: Hebron: an important city, and the name Hebron was also given to many people. A small city was also found with this name, though in a changed form in Hebrew.

3.1.4.en: This city is 18 miles south of Jerusalem, and the same distance north of Beersheba, and it still exists today.

3.1.5.en: Why do the descendants of David begin here with his sons in Hebron?

3.1.6.en: a. Since the two books of Chronicles focus on the joyful Kingdom of God, which is realized by the salvation that the Son of David offers, the First Book of Chronicles presented the person of David and his holy sons as types of the Lord Christ. So we are not surprised that the book does not refer to the glorious events in the life of David from his youth, when the Lord chose him to be king while he was still tending his father's sheep, and that was in secret, in the house of his father Jesse. The book also ignored the troubles that pursued David, especially from King Saul; what concerned it was the setting up of David as king over all the tribes in Hebron, to make him king over Israel.

3.1.7.en: "Hebron" is a Hebrew name meaning company, fellowship, bond, union, conjunction or marriage. What the book wishes to present as the starting point of the kingdom of Israel under the leadership of King David is that, as a representative of the Lord Christ, the King of kings, all the believers should be one holy company, bound by love and holiness, in constant fellowship together in Christ Jesus. We shall see later, especially in chapter 12, that "there was joy in Israel" (1 Chr 12:40), the secret of which was the cleaving of all the tribes, even the tribe of Benjamin, from which came King Saul, the opponent of David; it cleaved to him and to Judah even after the division of the kingdom, for Benjamin did not depart from Judah.

3.1.8.en: The kingdom of the Lord Christ rests on love, unity and fellowship; therefore it is fitting for the believer, in order to enjoy the divine Kingdom, that his heart open in love to all humanity.

3.1.9.en: The name "Hebron," then, offers us a practical indication of the true way to the heavenly royal wedding.

3.2.0.en: v The souls of all men and women are known to be brides of Christ, if they wish to keep bodily chastity and virginity of heart. Let them understand that Christ is the Bridegroom of their souls, not of their bodies[3].

3.2.1.en: Father Caesarius, Bishop of Arles b. Hebron took its fame because of famous events that took place in the days of the patriarchs. For example, when Sarah died in Hebron her husband Abraham bought the field of Ephron the Hittite which is in Machpelah, and buried her in a cave in the field, and it became a tomb for the family (Gen 23:19-20), and the cave still exists. A city was established in the valley, and Abraham, Isaac and Jacob each spent long periods in the region, and the three were buried in Hebron. If Hebron is the place of death and tombs, then there is need of a king who raises from the dead and challenges death.

3.2.2.en: It is as though the Son of David proclaims His glory by raising those who sleep in the graves of sins, that they may experience the pledge of eternity and accept the Son of David as the Door and the Way and the Life and the Resurrection and the Crown and the Treasure and the source of heavenly joy.

3.3.0.en: v He tasted death for all. And though by nature He Himself is Life, and is the Resurrection, He surrounded His body with death. And by His mighty power He trod down death in His body, to become the firstborn from the dead, and the firstborn of those who have fallen asleep... If the resurrection from the dead is said to come about through a man, and the man whom we know through it is the Word begotten of God, through Him the power of death was broken[4].

3.3.1.en: St. Cyril the Great c. From Hebron Joseph, rejected by his brothers, set out to seek his brothers (Gen 37:14); thus he was a type of the Lord Christ, who, being the Lord of all, did not disdain to become a firstborn brother to humanity, taking what is theirs (their humanity) and giving them what is His, partakers of the divine nature (2 Pet 1:4).

3.4.0.en: v When Paul calls the Corinthian Christians his brothers, he lays down a foundation of greater assurance. For we became brothers through the work of Christ in His earthly life and death. Above all this, what is the Gospel but the message that God became man, was crucified and rose? This the angel Gabriel proclaimed to the Virgin Mary (Lk 1:26-38), and it is what the prophets preached to the world, and what the Apostles proclaimed in truth[5].

3.4.1.en: St. John Chrysostom d. Hebron became a city of refuge (Josh 20:7), protecting the one who killed by mistake from the avenger of blood, so that he does not lay a hand on him until the high priest dies, and he lives in complete freedom, no one taking vengeance on him. It is as though Hebron points to the cross of the Lord Christ.

3.4.2.en: It is stated in the law of the cities of refuge that one who has killed unintentionally must flee quickly to the nearest city of refuge. Then he presents his case before the elders of the city, and they receive him among them if they see that he has confessed that he killed and have verified that the killing was done unintentionally, and not deliberately or with the intent to harm him. Then he returns to the city of refuge and stays within its walls, and the avenger, that is, the nearest kinsman of the slain, has no right to take vengeance for the blood of the slain. He remains so until the high priest dies, and then he has the right to leave the city, and the avenger has no right to approach him.

3.4.3.en: The death of the high priest points to the death of the Lord Christ, by whom we were released from the wages of sin, and who granted us complete freedom in Him. Since the city of refuge pointed to the Lord Christ, the repentant person remained safe as long as he was inside the Lord, but if he fled from Him he would be exposed to death.

3.4.4.en: v Tell me, let us see: when the high priest died, why did all the prisoners return to their borders?

3.5.0.en: This is the mystery of the High Priest who died on Golgotha, and by Him the two who went out of Eden returned, for they had been banished[6].

3.5.1.en: St. Mar Jacob of Sarug e. Hebron is the dwelling place of the priests, the sons of Aaron, until our Lord Jesus Christ, the heavenly High Priest after the order of Melchizedek (Ps 110:4), comes, who offered no animals, but offered His heart and conscience, as He offered bread and wine as a type of what the Lord of glory Jesus offers, turning the bread and wine into His Body and Blood which are given for us.

3.5.2.en: v When David clearly knew these (priests) in his prophecy, he did not liken any one of them to the Son.

3.5.3.en: He saw that all of them bring sacrifices that are not their own and are external to them, to offer them to God.

3.5.4.en: And he looked forward to the fact that Christ, when He willed and set out to become a priest, offered to His Father nothing external to Himself.

3.5.5.en: For King David looked at all the priests, who resembles the Son of God and who does not resemble Him.

3.5.6.en: He found that Melchizedek was made a priest without sacrifices, and did not pour out the blood of animals before God.

3.5.7.en: He did not bring the firstborn to the house of offering like Abel, nor offer a burnt offering of clean animals like Noah.

3.5.8.en: He did not slay (animals of) three years old before the Lord like Abraham (Gen 15:9), nor offer bulls and rams like the Levites.

3.5.9.en: He did not pour out the blood of turtledoves and young pigeons, nor make bulls and calves an offering (Ex 24; Lev 21:8; Lk 2:24).

3.5.10.en: But he stood before God with a pure heart and clean thoughts that rise above sacrifices.

3.5.11.en: He thought within himself to be pure like the offering, and to slay his mind, not animals, before God.

3.5.12.en: And to make no burnt offering to the Lord but himself, and for the pure conscience to be a sacrifice without stench.

3.5.13.en: (He said): I do not bring flesh to offer to the Lord, for He does not eat as food the sacrifice that is offered to Him.

3.5.14.en: It is an insult for animal sacrifices to be made to the Lord; I purify myself, and I slay my thought to God.

3.5.15.en: By these pure and lofty spiritual movements, the famous Melchizedek became a priest.

3.6.0.en: He was made a priest by the sufferings of his soul without sacrifices, and for this he was made like the Son of God[7].

3.6.1.en: St. Mar Jacob of Sarug f. The city of Hebron was known before Damascus, and its name was Kiriath-arba (Josh 14:15; 15:3; 21:11; Judg 1:10). It is stated in Joshua chapter 14 that Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite demanded his right, which the Lord had promised him by the tongue of Moses, which was to possess the mountain where the fortified cities were, and Hebron, which means "union" or "joining" or "company." Now when Caleb received "Hebron," which is also called "Kiriath-arba," "he drove thence the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak" (Josh 15:14). If Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite, who points to the heart that turned away from contempt and entered into glory, received Hebron as a reward, and thus entered into a holy and spiritual marriage or union, in which the soul is united with its Bridegroom forever, then Hebron on the other hand is called Kiriath-arba. The number 4 points to the world with its four directions: east and west, north and south, and it also points to the body taken from this earth or this world. So the one with a sanctified heart, who has turned to his eternal Bridegroom, reigns over his body, driving out from it the three sons of Anak, that the Lord may reign in it also. It is not enough that our hearts or inner lives be holy, but we must look upon our bodies with a holy look, for as we offer to the Bridegroom our inner hearts, so we offer Him our bodies, and the person works in his entirety in harmonious tone. St. Gregory of Nyssa likens the whole person to a lyre that bears different strings, yet which, by the Holy Spirit, presents a harmonious musical piece that rejoices the heart of God.

3.6.2.en: It is as though Hebron here, linked with its old name "Kiriath-arba," calls us to be sanctified in all our inner being as in our bodies, for the sake of the Son of David, the King of kings.

3.6.3.en: In brief we can say that if the two books urge us to come to know Christ the Redeemer and Savior, the bearer of the sins of the world, it emphasizes in particular His kingship.

3.6.4.en: g. Since Hebron points to union with the Lord Christ, the soul becomes a bride clinging to her Bridegroom, and forgets, with David, all her life with its dangerous deeds, such as the victory over Goliath the giant, and the women welcoming him with songs because he had rescued his country, and the rescuing of Saul from the evil spirit by playing the lyre with praises to the Lord, and Saul's battles against him, and Saul's continual plans to be rid of him. Nothing occupies the believer any longer except his clinging to the King of kings, and so he sees all the tribes coming to him to make him king over Israel. In a spirit of humility the believer looks with David in Hebron, in amazement, at how the Lord draws all mighty energies to work with Him for the sake of the Kingdom of God.

3.6.5.en: In Hebron David grows in humility, as he realizes that his installation as king is nothing but free divine grace, in which he has no merit, but it is the work of the Lord of Hosts for the glory of His holy name, for the sake of humanity, the object of His surpassing love.

3.6.6.en: Daniel: meaning "God judges," one of the sons of David by Abigail, who was born in Hebron (1 Chr 3:1). His name came as Chileab in (2 Sam 3:3), and some see that he had two names.

3.6.7.en: Abigail: her story is recorded in (1 Sam 25-30). A beautiful and virtuous wife, marked beside her beauty by her wisdom, who managed the wealth of her husband Nabal with wisdom. She was a successful counselor to her foolish husband, as also to David, for she prevented him from taking vengeance on Nabal.

3.6.8.en: She was not preoccupied with her husband's great wealth, nor with what she inherited from him, but gave herself and what she possessed to David, for she realized that he was a man of God. David the psalmist said to her: "Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, which sent thee this day to meet me: And blessed be thy advice, and blessed be thou, which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand" (1 Sam 25:32-33).

3.7.0.en: The third, Absalom the son of Maachah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur:

3.7.1.en: the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith: [2]

3.8.1.en: the sixth, Ithream by Eglah his wife. [3]

3.8.2.en: Absalom the son of Maachah: nothing is mentioned about him in Chronicles. He was handsome in appearance, with long hair, loved by his father and by the people. When his brother Amnon – from his father, not from his mother – assaulted Tamar his sister, and his father did not punish him, Absalom was greatly enraged, and had Amnon murdered by means of his servants. Absalom fled from the face of his father to King Geshur, the father of his mother (2 Sam 3:3; 13:37), and stayed there for three years, and when he returned to Jerusalem David refused to meet with him.

3.8.3.en: He used every means to draw the people to himself, and was able to proclaim his rebellion against his father and take over the throne. A battle took place between Absalom with his army and his father's army. As Absalom was riding on a mule, he went under the branches of a terebinth tree, and his head caught in a branch, so that he was hanging between heaven and earth (2 Sam 18:6-9). Joab aimed three darts at the heart of Absalom, although David had commanded the army commanders not to touch him. Ten young men of Moab struck him and killed him, and buried him in a great pit, and raised over him a great heap of stones, as a kind of public disgrace of rebels and criminals.

3.8.4.en: David grieved greatly for him and lamented him, but he was compelled to meet the army returning victorious, so that the people would not rise up against him.

3.8.5.en: David had been anointed king over all Israel in Hebron (1 Sam 2:1-4, 11), and made it his royal center; sadly his son Absalom, who was of his own loins, rebelled against David in Hebron!

3.8.6.en: Talmai king of Geshur: a Semitic name meaning "belonging to furrows or the plowman." It is likely derived from the Hurrian word "talma'" meaning "great."

3.8.7.en: Shephatiah of Abital: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has executed judgment," and he is the fifth son of David (1 Chr 3:3), who was born in Hebron of Abital.

3.8.8.en: Adonijah the son of Haggith, or Adonijah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is Lord" or "the Lord is Master."

3.8.9.en: Ithream: a Hebrew name meaning "the uncle is generous," a son of David born in Hebron (1 Chr 3:3).

3.9.0.en: These six were born unto him in Hebron;

3.9.1.en: and there he reigned seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years. [4]

3.10.s.en: 2. The descendants of David in Jerusalem

3.10.0.en: 5 And these were born unto him in Jerusalem; Shimea, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon, four, of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel: 6 Ibhar also, and Elishama, and Eliphelet, 7 And Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia, 8 And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine. 9 These were all the sons of David, beside the sons of the concubines, and Tamar their sister.

3.10.1.en: The book moves us from the city of Hebron, as the beginning of the kingdom of David over all Israel, to the city of Jerusalem as the city of God or the holy city (Neh 11:1, 16; Mt 4:5). The contemporary Arabs call it al-Quds. As for the origin of the Hebrew word, it is disputed; some see that it means possession of peace or foundation of peace. Heaven itself has been called "Jerusalem which is above" (Gal 4:26).

3.10.2.en: If the beginning of the way to enjoy the Kingdom of Christ is union and fellowship with God and people (Hebron), then the end of the way is the enjoyment of eternal, heavenly peace. This is the way to which the two books of Chronicles point.

3.10.3.en: Perhaps the most important matters that concern us in Jerusalem are the following:

3.10.4.en: a. It was anciently called Salem, and its king was Melchizedek, after whose order appeared the Lord Christ, the heavenly High Priest, who by His blood carries us to the bosom of the Father, justified.

3.10.5.en: b. Jerusalem was linked with Mount Moriah, which Abraham reached on the third day after setting out from Beersheba with his son Isaac to offer him as a sacrifice (Gen 22), and he returned with him alive, for the number three points to the resurrection of the Lord Christ.

3.10.6.en: c. In Jerusalem Solomon built the Temple as a sign of the constant divine presence in the midst of His people. It is as though Jerusalem urges us to enjoy the Lord Christ as the Priest-King (after the order of Melchizedek), and as the sacrifice that bestows righteousness and resurrection, and to enjoy fellowship with God.

3.10.7.en: And these were born unto him in Jerusalem;

3.10.8.en: Shimea, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,

3.10.9.en: four, of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel. [5]

3.10.10.en: These were born in Jerusalem, and they are mentioned in (2 Sam 5:14-16; 1 Chr 14:4-7), but we find a difference in the names.

3.10.11.en: Shimea appears in Samuel and in (1 Chr 14) as Shammua.

3.11.0.en: Elishama [6]: appears in Samuel and in (1 Chr 14) as Elishua.

3.12.0.en: Eliada [8]: appears in (1 Chr 14) as Beeliada, and the two names carry the same meaning, "the Lord knows."

3.12.1.en: The Book of Samuel did not mention Eliphelet [6] and Nogah [7], and perhaps they died young.

3.12.2.en: Shobab: a Hebrew name meaning "backsliding." He is the son of Bathshua by David, born in Jerusalem.

3.12.3.en: Nathan: a Hebrew name meaning "God has given."

3.12.4.en: Bath-shua: a corruption of Bathsheba, a Hebrew name meaning "daughter of the oath" or "daughter of the seventh day." Her story is recorded in (2 Sam 11-12; 1 Kgs 1). David fell into sin with her, and summoned her husband Uriah the Hittite, who was a commander in the army, loyal and faithful to David and to the children of Israel, and asked him to spend the night in his house, but he refused to sleep with his wife while the army was in battle. David arranged his killing in the army so that his error would not be exposed. God sent to David Nathan the prophet, who rebuked him and declared to him the chastisements of the Lord for him. Her son Solomon the Wise took the throne after his father David, and built the Temple (1 Kgs 1-11; 2 Chr 2-9).

3.12.5.en: Ammiel: he was also called Eliam (2 Sam 11:3).

3.13.0.en: And Ibhar, and Elishama, and Eliphelet [6]

3.13.1.en: Ibhar: a Hebrew name meaning "he chooses," one of the sons of David, born in Jerusalem.

3.13.2.en: Elishama: a Hebrew name meaning "God has heard," which appears in (2 Sam 5:16; 1 Chr 14) as "Elishama." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A son of David, who was born in Jerusalem (1 Chr 3:1, 5-6). 2. Another son of David (1 Chr 3:8).

3.13.3.en: Eliphelet: a Hebrew name meaning "God has delivered him," which appears in (2 Sam 5:16; 1 Chr 14) as "Eliphalet." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A son of David, born in Jerusalem (1 Chr 3:5-6, 14; 14:5). 2. Another son of David, also born in Jerusalem, and perhaps after the death of the previous son.

3.14.0.en: And Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia, [7]

3.14.1.en: Nogah: a Hebrew name meaning "brightness," and he is one of the sons of David.

3.15.0.en: And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine. [8]

3.15.1.en: Eliada: a Hebrew name meaning "one who knows God", a son of David born in Jerusalem.

3.15.2.en: Eliphelet: a son of David other than Eliphalet, and perhaps after Eliphalet died his brother was born and was called by his name, with a change in his name.

3.15.3.en: Japhia: a Semitic name meaning "he shines."

3.16.0.en: These were all the sons of David, beside the sons of the concubines,

3.16.2.en: David had concubines, the names of whose sons are not mentioned, and perhaps the reason for this is that the concubines committed a kind of betrayal of David in the matter of Absalom.

3.16.3.en: Tamar: David had other daughters besides Tamar; Tamar is mentioned because of the incident concerning her brother Amnon. She was marked by beauty; Amnon her brother by her father assaulted her, and as much as he loved her exceedingly, so that he became sick because of his love for her, he hated her after assaulting her, and drove her from his presence, and so shame fell upon her (2 Sam 13-14).

3.17.0.en: 10 And Solomon's son was Rehoboam, Abia his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son, 11 Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son, 12 Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son, 13 Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son, 14 Amon his son, Josiah his son. 15 And the sons of Josiah were, the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum. 16 And the sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son. 17 And the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son, 18 Malchiram also, and Pedaiah, and Shenazar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah. 19 And the sons of Pedaiah were, Zerubbabel, and Shimei: and the sons of Zerubbabel; Meshullam, and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister: 20 And Hashubah, and Ohel, and Berechiah, and Hasadiah, Jushabhesed, five. 21 And the sons of Hananiah; Pelatiah, and Jesaiah: the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shechaniah. 22 And the sons of Shechaniah; Shemaiah: and the sons of Shemaiah; Hattush, and Igeal, and Bariah, and Neariah, and Shaphat, six. 23 And the sons of Neariah; Elioenai, and Hezekiah, and Azrikam, three. 24 And the sons of Elioenai were, Hodaiah, and Eliashib, and Pelaiah, and Akkub, and Johanan, and Dalaiah, and Anani, seven.

3.17.1.en: Sadly, among the sons of David there were those who caused him great bitterness, such as Amnon, Absalom and Adonijah. And we have not heard of any of his sons who imitated his godliness except Solomon, though Solomon himself went astray because of his marriage to pagan women.

3.17.2.en: Solomon, who was the fourth son of Bathsheba among those born in Jerusalem, sat on the throne, and the descendants of Solomon came in harmony with what is stated in the First and Second Books of Kings and what is stated during the exile and the return from it.

3.17.3.en: And Solomon's son was Rehoboam, Abia his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son, [10]

3.17.4.en: Rehoboam: he took the kingdom after the death of his father. He was narrow in thinking, and so he caused the division of the kingdom, for he answered harshly those who asked him to lighten the yoke with which his father had burdened them. This was done on the counsel of the young men who had grown up with him, and he rejected the counsel of the elders, the counselors of his father. Jeroboam exploited the matter, and gathered around him ten tribes under the name of the kingdom of Israel, and Judah and Benjamin remained with Rehoboam under the name of the kingdom of Judah.

3.17.5.en: The war continued between the two kingdoms for a long time, and often one of the two kingdoms allied itself with a foreign kingdom such as Aram or Assyria against its sister. Many of the descendants of Solomon took the rule in the kingdom of Judah, and we have previously spoken about these kings in Second Kings and Second Chronicles.

3.17.7.en: Jehoshaphat (2 Chr 17-20): It seems that he learned from his father Asa, and imitated his good works, but on many occasions we see him imitating his father in his evil. He often returned to the Lord seeking His counsel and succeeded, but he allowed his son to marry Athaliah the daughter of Ahab the wicked king of Israel, who was an image of her mother, the wicked Jezebel.

3.18.0.en: Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son, [11]

3.19.0.en: Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son, [12]

3.19.1.en: Azariah (Uzziah) (2 Chr 26): he was a successful king, who made many accomplishments, succeeded in wars and in time of peace, and was marked by building up and sound planning. Sadly his desire drove him not to give thanks to God but to fall into pride. He tried to seize the priestly work, and was struck with leprosy. He also failed to remove many symbols of idolatry from the country.

3.20.0.en: Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son, [13]

3.20.1.en: King Hezekiah: we have previously spoken about him in (2 Kgs 18-20).

3.21.0.en: Amon his son, Josiah his son. [14]

3.21.1.en: King Josiah: we have previously spoken about him in (2 Kgs 22-23).

3.22.0.en: And the sons of Josiah were, the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum. [15]

3.22.1.en: From verse 15 onward, after the reign of the devoted and faithful Josiah, we find the kings at the time of the final ruin of Judah. This group brought the kingdom to the exile.

3.22.2.en: In the genealogies of Jesus Christ (Mt 1) Hananiah, Shechaniah, Neariah, Elioenai and Hodaiah are not mentioned. Some see that the rulers of Babylon changed these names in order to blot out every trace of monarchy from the spirit of the Jewish exiles (Dan 1:6-7)[8].

3.22.3.en: Johanan: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is gracious." More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The firstborn of Josiah, though he did not take the throne. Johanan is mentioned only here, and perhaps he died in his youth. 2. A son of Elioenai, of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:24).

3.22.4.en: Jehoiakim: he is Eliakim (2 Kgs 23:34). (See Jer 22-28; 35-36).

3.22.5.en: Zedekiah: he is the fourth, and his first name was Mattaniah (2 Kgs 24:17). See (Jer 21-39).

3.22.6.en: Shallum: he is Jehoahaz (2 Kgs 23:30), and he is the third of the brothers, though he is mentioned last.

3.23.0.en: And the sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son. [16]

3.23.1.en: Jeconiah: he is Coniah in (Jer 22:24, 28; 37:1); it means "He establishes" or "the Lord establishes."

3.23.2.en: Zedekiah: some see that the word "his son" here means "his successor." Zedekiah here is Zedekiah the son of Josiah, the king who succeeded Jehoiachin, and he is mentioned here because he did not go into exile.

3.24.0.en: And the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son, [17]

3.24.1.en: Assir: a Hebrew word meaning "captive," and some thought that this name means a description of Jeconiah as "the captive," but it is clear from the Hebrew text and from the ancient versions that it does not indicate a description but a proper name.

3.24.2.en: Salathiel or Shealtiel: a Hebrew name meaning "I asked of God," and he is the son of Neri (Lk 3:27), adopted by Jeconiah after his late exile in March 597 B.C.

3.25.0.en: Malchiram also, and Pedaiah, and Shenazar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah. [18]

3.25.1.en: Malchiram: a Hebrew name meaning "the king is exalted," and he is the son of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) king of Judah.

3.25.2.en: Pedaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has redeemed," and it is the name of the brother of Salathiel and the father of Zerubbabel.

3.25.3.en: Shenazar[9]: of the descendants of Jeconiah. He is equivalent to "Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah at the return from Babylon in (538/537 B.C.) (Ezra 1:8). Both are an abbreviation of the Akkadian word Sin-aba-usur, which means: "Protect me, O moon god (Bassar)." He succeeded his nephew Zerubbabel, the natural son of the next older brother Pedaiah, but who was legally ascribed to the eldest son Salathiel (Ezra 3:2; Hag 1:1, 12; Mt 1:12; Lk 3:27). For Salathiel probably died without having offspring, therefore his brother raised up offspring for him to be ascribed to him according to the Law (Deut 25:5-10).

3.25.4.en: Jecamiah or Jekamiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh rises up," a man of Judah of the royal line.

3.25.5.en: Hoshama: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has heard," and he is one of the descendants of King Jeconiah.

3.25.6.en: Nedabiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is generous," and he is a son of King Jeconiah.

3.26.0.en: And the sons of Pedaiah were, Zerubbabel, and Shimei:

3.26.1.en: and the sons of Zerubbabel; Meshullam, and Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister: [19]

3.26.2.en: Zerubbabel: an Akkadian name meaning "sown in Babylon" or "born in Babylon," the son of Salathiel. Salathiel died without offspring, and perhaps Pedaiah his brother took his wife and raised up offspring for his brother according to the Law, so Zerubbabel became a son to him.

3.26.3.en: The leader of the first group of those returning from the captivity of Babylon to Jerusalem by the decree of Cyrus. Cyrus sent him in the sixth century B.C., and financed his project, and brought back with him the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar had seized from the Temple. He began by building the altar for the worship of God, and laid foundations of the Temple. Two problems arose. The first was that some of the elders grieved when they compared the Temple that Solomon had previously built with the Temple that Zerubbabel rebuilt. And the second problem was that some enemies infiltrated and stopped the work by political pressure. So some were occupied with building their own houses, saying that the time had not come to build the house of the Lord. So God sent the prophets Haggai and Zechariah to encourage Zerubbabel, and the work began again after 16 years and the Temple was completed in four years. He was not like Nehemiah, for the latter did not allow problems and opposition to stop him from building.

3.26.4.en: The message of the Lord to him: "Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts. Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it" (Zech 4:6-7).

3.26.5.en: In [19] two sons and their sister are mentioned, and in [21] five. Perhaps these five were from another mother, or were born after the return from the exile.

3.26.6.en: Shimei: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh hears," and he is the brother of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:19).

3.26.7.en: Meshullam: a Hebrew name meaning "one who has received his recompense," and it is the name of one of the sons of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:19).

3.26.8.en: Hananiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has shown favor, has been gracious." He is the son of Zerubbabel, and the father of Pelatiah and Jesaiah.

3.26.9.en: Shelomith or Shelomoth: the feminine of "Shelomi" or "Solomon," and she is the daughter of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:19).

3.27.0.en: And Hashubah, and Ohel, and Berechiah, and Hasadiah, Jushabhesed, five. [20]

3.27.1.en: Hashubah: a Hebrew name meaning "reckoned or measure," and he is a son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:20).

3.27.2.en: Ohel: a Hebrew name meaning "tent," and he is one of the sons of Zerubbabel (1 Chr 3:20).

3.27.3.en: Berechiah: a Hebrew name meaning "blessed of God." A son of Zerubbabel, of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:20).

3.27.4.en: Hasadiah: a Hebrew name meaning "the Lord has been gracious," and he is a son of Zerubbabel, of the royal line of David.

3.27.5.en: Jushab or Jushabhesed: a Hebrew name meaning "mercy is repaid," and he is a son of Zerubbabel, of the descendants of David.

3.28.0.en: And the sons of Hananiah; Pelatiah, and Jesaiah: the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shechaniah. [21]

3.28.1.en: Pelatiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has set free," one of the sons of Hananiah, and a grandson of Zerubbabel.

3.28.2.en: Jesaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has saved." A son of Hananiah, of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:21).

3.28.3.en: Rephaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh has healed." A man of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:21).

3.28.4.en: Arnan or Araunah: the meaning of the Hebrew word is not known with certainty.

3.28.5.en: Obadiah: a Hebrew name meaning "servant of Yahweh," and he is a head of a house of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:21).

3.28.6.en: Shechaniah: an Aramaic word meaning "Yahweh dwells." Of the descendants of David, and the founder of a family.

3.29.0.en: And the sons of Shechaniah; Shemaiah: and the sons of Shemaiah; Hattush, and Igeal, and Bariah, and Neariah, and Shaphat, six. [22]

3.29.1.en: Shemaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "God hears." He is a son of David by Bathshua.

3.29.2.en: Hattush: a Hebrew name meaning "gathered." A man of Judah, the son of Shemaiah, and of the family of Shechaniah.

3.29.3.en: Igeal: a Hebrew name meaning "he redeems." He is the son of Shemaiah, of the descendants of King Shechaniah (1 Chr 3:22).

3.29.4.en: Bariah: a Hebrew name meaning "fugitive or wanderer."

3.29.5.en: Neariah: a Hebrew name meaning "bearer of the shield of Yahweh," and he is the father of Elioenai, Hezekiah and Azrikam, one of the six sons of Shemaiah, of the descendants of Solomon (1 Chr 3:22-23).

3.29.6.en: Shaphat: a Hebrew name meaning "he has judged." A son of Shemaiah, of the descendants of King David of the tribe of Judah.

3.30.0.en: And the sons of Neariah; Elioenai, and Hezekiah, and Azrikam, three. [23]

3.30.1.en: Elioenai: a Hebrew name meaning "my eyes are toward Yahweh," and he is a son of Neariah of the tribe of Judah.

3.30.2.en: Hezekiah: a Hebrew name meaning "the Lord has strengthened" or "the Lord is strength." He is a son of Neariah, a relative of the royal family of Judah (1 Chr 3:23).

3.30.3.en: Azrikam: a Hebrew name meaning "my help has arisen," and he is a son of Neariah Elioenai, one of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:23).

3.30.4.en: And the sons of Elioenai were,

3.31.0.en: Hodaiah, and Eliashib, and Pelaiah, and Akkub, and Johanan, and Dalaiah, and Anani, seven. [24]

3.31.1.en: Hod: a Hebrew name meaning "splendor," and Hodaiah means "splendor to Yahweh," and he is a son of Elioenai, one of the descendants of David (1 Chr 3:24).

3.31.2.en: Eliashib: a Hebrew name meaning "he whom God restores." He is a son of Elioenai, of the descendants of Zerubbabel.

3.31.3.en: Pelaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "Yahweh is wonderful," and it is the name of a man of Judah, of the descendants of Shechaniah.

3.31.4.en: Akkub: a Hebrew name meaning "follower or pursuer," a son of Elioenai from among the line of Shechaniah, of the descendants of David.

3.31.5.en: Dalaiah: a Hebrew name meaning "he whom the Lord has freed," and he is of the descendants of David, a son of Elioenai.

3.31.6.en: Anani: a Hebrew name, an abbreviation of the name "Ananiah," one of the seven sons of Elioenai, of the descendants of David.

3.31.7.en: Bring me into the eternal wedding, that I may enjoy fellowship in Your glories

3.31.8.en: v May Your Holy Spirit carry me with David to Hebron.

3.31.9.en: In amazement I stand to see my father David, while under the shadow of the Law, setting out to Hebron, the symbol of the wedding and union and clinging to You.

3.31.10.en: He is not preoccupied with all the events of his past; he remembers only his glorious works through You, and his weaknesses and bitter trials.

3.31.11.en: He no longer remembers King Saul's continual opposition to him.

3.31.12.en: His spiritual wedding and his enjoyment of the splendor of Your glory in him drew away all his feelings!

3.31.13.en: v As is his habit, he did not reproach You:

3.31.14.en: Where is Your promise to me, when I was a boy, that I would become king over all Israel?

3.31.15.en: What occupies him is to enjoy You, O King of kings.

3.31.16.en: He sees You by the spirit of prophecy on the cross as King!

3.31.17.en: Your love and glory drew all his thoughts and emotions and senses!

3.31.18.en: It suffices him to see You, O Savior of the world, uniting the heavenly and the human together.

3.31.19.en: v His meeting with You wrought wonder in all the mighty men.

3.31.20.en: The brothers of Saul the wicked and the commanders of his army withdrew to You.

3.31.21.en: They were turned into working energies for the sake of Your Kingdom.

3.31.22.en: They see in You the wonderful King who is in the bosom of the King of kings.

3.31.23.en: They see in You a fatherhood that is a shadow of the fatherhood of God, full of tenderness.

3.31.24.en: v In Hebron is the tomb of Sarah and Abraham and Jacob and Isaac.

3.31.25.en: They smell the fragrant and beautiful scent of Your resurrection, instead of the smell of death and corruption.

3.31.26.en: All the tribes saw You as they were coming to David.

3.31.27.en: They enjoyed You, You who shone with the splendor of the resurrection upon the heart of David.

3.31.28.en: Hebron is no longer a center for visiting the tombs of the great, but has become a shadow of the heavenly wedding.

3.31.29.en: The dead and the living enjoy it in the fellowship of the heavenly ones, no, rather in fellowship and enjoyment of the Holy Trinity!

3.31.30.en: v Hebron is no longer the dwelling of the priests and Levites, but has become a shadow of the bridal chambers of the heavenly High Priest and of the throne of the King of kings.

3.31.31.en: They see You as in the heavenly sanctuaries interceding with Your blood for humanity.

3.31.32.en: v Praise and thanks be to You, for You enter with me into Hebron.

3.31.33.en: My soul rests, not only because it is a city of refuge, but because it has become for me a place of meeting with You, O fortress of my life.

3.31.34.en: v Grant me, with David, to set out from Hebron to Jerusalem.

3.31.35.en: Truly, what shall I say? And of what shall I speak concerning the holy city of God?

3.31.36.en: Founded on mountains, not of stone, but heavenly.

3.31.37.en: What enemy can infiltrate it, and what harm can reach it!

3.31.38.en: v Anciently Jerusalem was called Salem, and its king was Melchizedek.

3.31.39.en: Grant me to enjoy the pledge of the Jerusalem above; You are its King, the Giver of true righteousness and heavenly peace.

3.31.40.en: v Jerusalem takes pride in its Temple, but the Jerusalem above, its temple is not made with human hands.

3.31.41.en: You are its sun and its light; there is no place in it for darkness.

3.31.42.en: You are the mystery of its glory and its delight and its joy.

3.31.43.en: Through You I cross over to it, and live in Your divine embrace.

3.31.44.en: v With my father David I sing, saying:

3.31.45.en: I have known You, O Son of David, Bridegroom of my soul!

3.31.46.en: You are the King of kings, You make me a king!

3.31.47.en: You are the Resurrection, You grant me victory over death!

3.31.48.en: You are the heavenly High Priest, You enter with me into the bosom of the Father!

3.31.49.en: You are my divine, heavenly refuge!

3.31.50.en: You carry me to heaven, the Jerusalem above!

3.31.51.en: Your divine peace descends upon me, and You cover me with Your righteousness, O Holy One!

3.31.52.en: I enjoy the splendor of the heavenly sanctuaries.

3.31.53.en: You shine upon me with Your light, so darkness will not surround me!

3.31.54.en: You are my glory and my joy, O delight of my soul!
